s:
Consider the following statements about the PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PM-DDKY):
1. It was launched on 11 October 2025, after Union Cabinet approval on 16 July 2025.
2. It runs for four years, from 2025-26 to 2028-29.
3. It covers 100 districts picked on low productivity, low cropping intensity and low credit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: PM-DDKY runs for six years, 2025-26 to 2030-31. Statements 1 and 3 are correct: launched 11 October 2025 (Cabinet approval 16 July 2025) and it covers 100 low-productivity districts chosen on low productivity, low cropping intensity and low credit.

s:
Consider the following statements about the PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana:
1. Its nodal body is NITI Aayog.
2. It converges 36 schemes of 11 Ministries/Departments.
3. It is modelled on the Aspirational Districts Programme launched in January 2018.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 1 is wrong: the nodal ministry is the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (NITI Aayog only ran the Aspirational Districts Programme on which it is modelled). Statements 2 (36 schemes of 11 Ministries/Departments) and 3 (modelled on the Aspirational Districts Programme, Jan 2018) are correct - so only two.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY):
1. It was launched on 10 September 2020 and replaced the Blue Revolution Scheme.
2. India's fish production rose to 197.75 lakh tonnes in 2024-25.
3. Its 100 Climate Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages get 50% central funding.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: the 100 Climate Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages get 100% central funding. Statements 1 (launched 10 Sep 2020, replaced the Blue Revolution Scheme) and 2 (197.75 lakh t in 2024-25, up from 141.64 lakh t in 2019-20) are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements about PM-KISAN:
1. It gives ₹6,000 a year in three instalments of ₹2,000 by DBT to Aadhaar-linked bank accounts.
2. Its 24th instalment (31 October 2026) released over ₹28,690 crore.
3. It was launched on 24 February 2019 but made effective from 1 December 2018.
4. Its 24th instalment reached 9.34 crore farmers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: the 24th instalment released over ₹18,690 crore (not ₹28,690 crore) to 9.34 crore farmers. Statements 1 (₹6,000 a year, three ₹2,000 instalments by DBT to Aadhaar-linked accounts), 3 (launched 24 Feb 2019, effective 1 Dec 2018) and 4 are correct.

s:
Assertion (A): PM-KISAN is a Central Sector Scheme.
Reason (R): PM-KISAN is funded 100% by the Centre.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: PM-KISAN is a Central Sector Scheme of the Ministry of Agriculture precisely because the Centre bears 100% of its cost (a Centrally Sponsored Scheme would share cost with States).

s:
Consider the following statements about the Bharat Bovine Breeding and Research Centre inaugurated on 1 November 2026:
1. It was inaugurated at Anand, Gujarat.
2. It was set up by Banas Dairy with NDDB guidance under the Rashtriya Gokul Mission.
3. The Rashtriya Gokul Mission was launched in December 2014.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is wrong: the ₹325 crore centre is at Bhildi, Banaskantha, Gujarat - Anand is the headquarters of NDDB. Statements 2 (Banas Dairy with NDDB guidance under the Rashtriya Gokul Mission) and 3 (RGM, Dec 2014) are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ladakh was declared India's first 100% organic Union Territory on 25 October 2026 by Lt Governor V. K. Saxena.
2. Sale and use of chemical fertilisers were banned in Ladakh from January 2026.
3. Sikkim became India's first organic State in 2016.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: chemical fertilisers were banned in Ladakh from July 2026. Statements 1 (declared 25 Oct 2026 by LG V. K. Saxena) and 3 (Sikkim, first organic State, 2016) are correct.

s:
Match List I (nutrition initiative) with List II (date):
List I
a. POSHAN Abhiyaan
b. Poshan Tracker
c. 9th Rashtriya Poshan Maah
d. 8th Poshan Pakhwada
List II
i. 9 September 2026
ii. March 2018
iii. 9-23 April 2026
iv. 1 March 2021
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: POSHAN Abhiyaan - March 2018 (Jhunjhunu); Poshan Tracker - 1 March 2021; 9th Rashtriya Poshan Maah - launched 9 September 2026 at Varanasi; 8th Poshan Pakhwada - 9-23 April 2026. So a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 9th Rashtriya Poshan Maah (2026) and nutrition missions:
1. It was launched from Dhar, Madhya Pradesh.
2. Its theme was "Hamari Anganwadi, Hamari Jimmedari".
3. Ten years of PMMVY was among its priorities.
4. Mission Poshan 2.0, announced in Budget 2021-22, is run by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 1 is wrong: the 9th Poshan Maah was launched on 9 Sep 2026 at the Rudraksh Centre, Varanasi; Dhar, MP was the launch venue of the 8th Poshan Maah (2025). Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct - so only three.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. 'Hidden hunger' means a deficiency of micronutrients such as iron, iodine, zinc and vitamins.
2. According to the WHO (September 2026), India has about one-half of the world's undernutrition.
3. India developed 152 biofortified crop varieties during 2014-2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: India has about one-third (not one-half) of global undernutrition. Statement 1 (hidden hunger = micronutrient deficiency) and statement 3 (152 biofortified varieties, 2014-2024) are correct.

s:
With reference to rice fortification in India, consider the following statements:
1. The 2019 pilot fortified rice with iron, folic acid and vitamin B12.
2. From March 2024, all custom-milled rice in PDS, ICDS, PM-POSHAN and PMGKAY was fortified.
3. In February 2026, the supply of fortified rice was stopped under all these schemes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: in February 2026 fortified rice was temporarily stopped under PMGKAY only. Statements 1 (2019 pilot - iron, folic acid, vitamin B12) and 2 (March 2024 - all custom-milled rice in PDS, ICDS, PM-POSHAN, PMGKAY) are correct.

s:
Match List I with List II:
List I
a. Food Corporation of India
b. National Food Security Act, 2013
c. National Dairy Development Board
d. International Year of the Woman Farmer 2026
List II
i. Headquarters at Anand
ii. Lead agency FAO
iii. Established 14 January 1965
iv. Covers 75% rural and 50% urban population
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: FCI - established 14 January 1965; NFSA 2013 - 75% rural and 50% urban coverage; NDDB (est. 1965) - HQ Anand; International Year of the Woman Farmer 2026 - lead agency FAO. So a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

s:
Consider the following statements about ULLAS - Nav Bharat Saksharta Karyakram:
1. ULLAS stands for Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society and targets adults aged 15 years and above.
2. Its slogan is "Padhe Bharat, Badhe Bharat".
3. Adult learners are assessed through FLNAT.
4. A unit is treated as 'fully literate' at 95% literacy or more.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: the ULLAS slogan is "Jan Jan Sakshar". Statements 1 (full form; adults 15+), 3 (FLNAT test) and 4 (fully literate = at least 95%) are correct.

s:
Match List I (State/UT) with List II (literacy milestone under ULLAS):
List I
a. Ladakh
b. Mizoram
c. Uttarakhand
d. Lakshadweep
List II
i. 11 October 2026 - first UT with 100% literacy
ii. June 2024 - first UT fully functionally literate
iii. July 2026 - declared fully literate
iv. 20 May 2025 - first State fully literate
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Ladakh - first UT fully functionally literate (June 2024); Mizoram - first State fully literate (20 May 2025); Uttarakhand - fully literate in July 2026; Lakshadweep - first UT with 100% literacy (11 Oct 2026). So a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.

s:
Consider the following statements about literacy and learning data:
1. According to PLFS 2025, India's overall literacy rate is 81.1%, against 74.04% in Census 2011.
2. The Annual Status of Education Report (ASER) is brought out by NCERT.
3. As per ASER 2024, 23.4% of Class III government-school students could read a Class II text.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: ASER is brought out by Pratham, an NGO, not NCERT. Statements 1 (PLFS 2025 81.1%; Census 2011 74.04%) and 3 (ASER 2024 - 23.4%) are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. NIPUN Bharat aims at foundational literacy and numeracy by Grade 2, with a target of 2026-27.
2. Samagra Shiksha merged Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, RMSA and Teacher Education.
3. International Literacy Day is observed on 8 September.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: NIPUN Bharat - FLN by Grade 2, target 2026-27; Samagra Shiksha merged SSA, RMSA and Teacher Education; International Literacy Day - 8 September.

s:
Consider the following statements about PM SHRI (Pradhan Mantri Schools for Rising India):
1. It was launched on 7 September 2022 as a Central Sector Scheme of the Ministry of Education.
2. It targets more than 14,500 schools.
3. Its total cost is ₹27,360 crore, of which the central share is ₹18,128 crore.
4. Schools are selected through a 3-stage Challenge Mode using UDISE+.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 1 is wrong: PM SHRI (launched 7 Sep 2022) is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, not Central Sector. Statements 2 (14,500+ schools), 3 (₹27,360 crore, central share ₹18,128 crore) and 4 (3-stage Challenge Mode, UDISE+) are correct - so only three.

s:
Match List I with List II as per AISHE 2023-24:
List I
a. Universities
b. Colleges
c. Enrolment
d. Female GER
List II
i. 4.50 crore
ii. 31.2%
iii. 1,289
iv. 48,246
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: AISHE 2023-24: 1,289 universities, 48,246 colleges, enrolment 4.50 crore, female GER 31.2% (male 28.9%). So a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii. Swapping universities and colleges is the common trap.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The UGC is a statutory body set up under the UGC Act, 1956.
2. Under the UGC (Foreign HEI Campuses) Regulations 2023, a foreign university should generally be in the global top 200.
3. The University of Colorado Denver got a Letter of Intent for Hyderabad, the first foreign university campus in Telangana.
4. Birkbeck, University of London got a Letter of Approval for a campus in Bengaluru.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: the 2023 Regulations generally require a place in the global top 500. Statements 1 (UGC Act, 1956), 3 (Colorado Denver - Hyderabad, first in Telangana) and 4 (Birkbeck - Bengaluru, Sep 2026) are correct - so only three.

s:
Match List I (institute) with List II (first / initiative, 2026):
List I
a. IIT Hyderabad
b. IIT Ropar
c. IIT Mandi
d. IIT (ISM) Dhanbad
List II
i. Science on Wheels for rural schools
ii. Hosts TEXMiN
iii. India's first 'Goodness' credit course
iv. India's first thesis-free PhD
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: IIT Hyderabad - first 'Goodness' credit course; IIT Ropar - first thesis-free PhD; IIT Mandi (Kamand) - 'Science on Wheels'; IIT (ISM) Dhanbad - TEXMiN (which signed an SoI with NITI Aayog). So a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

s:
Assertion (A): IITs are Institutes of National Importance.
Reason (R): IITs are governed by the UGC Act, 1956.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is true but R is false: IITs are Institutes of National Importance under the Institutes of Technology Act, 1961; the UGC Act, 1956 only set up the UGC.

s:
Consider the following statements about the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan:
1. It was launched on 13 October 2021 and its nodal body is DPIIT.
2. Its seven sectors include Waterways, Airports and Mass Transport.
3. Its Inter-ministerial body ITLA appraises central projects of ₹1,000 crore or more.
4. The National Logistics Policy was launched on 17 September 2022.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: ITLA appraises central projects of ₹500 crore or more. Statements 1 (13 Oct 2021, DPIIT), 2 (seven sectors: Railways, Roads, Ports, Waterways, Airports, Mass Transport, Logistics - not telecom) and 4 (NLP, 17 Sep 2022) are correct.

s:
Assertion (A): Telecommunications is one of the seven sectors of the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan.
Reason (R): PM Gati Shakti is a GIS-based platform with DPIIT as its nodal body.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is false: the seven sectors are Railways, Roads, Ports, Waterways, Airports, Mass Transport and Logistics Infrastructure - not telecom. R is true: it is a GIS-based platform with DPIIT as nodal body.

s:
Consider the following statements about the UDAN scheme:
1. It was launched on 21 October 2017.
2. The first UDAN flight was on the Shimla-Delhi route on 27 April 2017.
3. By its 10th anniversary it had 687 routes and 95 airports.
4. Modified UDAN was launched at Jodhpur Airport on 4 July 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statement 1 is wrong: UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik) was launched on 21 October 2016 - the first flight (Shimla-Delhi, 27 April 2017) came after. Statements 2, 3 (687 routes, 95 airports) and 4 (Modified UDAN, Jodhpur, 4 July 2026; ₹28,840 crore for 10 years) are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Samudra Manthan Scheme (guidelines October 2026):
1. It is a ₹84,084 crore scheme of the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
2. It supports 56 exploratory and 4 stratigraphic wells.
3. It meets up to 50% of drilling cost, subject to ₹675 crore per well.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is wrong: the ₹84,084 crore scheme for deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploration is of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. Statements 2 (56 exploratory + 4 stratigraphic wells) and 3 (up to 50%, max ₹675 crore per well) are correct.

s:
Match List I (scheme) with List II (outlay):
List I
a. Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme
b. Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme
c. Samudra Manthan Scheme
d. Modified UDAN
List II
i. ₹10,000 crore
ii. ₹28,840 crore
iii. ₹1,856.67 crore
iv. ₹84,084 crore
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme - ₹1,856.67 crore; Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme - ₹10,000 crore; Samudra Manthan - ₹84,084 crore; Modified UDAN - ₹28,840 crore for 10 years. So a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.

s:
Consider the following statements about the schemes approved by the Union Cabinet on 29 October 2026:
1. The Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme is under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
2. The Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme runs up to FY 2039-40 and covers Greenfield and Brownfield units.
3. Sports Goods Manufacturing Zones under the Khelo India scheme will use BHAVYA Scheme infrastructure.
4. Meerut and Jalandhar are named as sports-goods hubs.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 1 is wrong: the ₹10,000 crore CMPS is under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways. Statements 2 (up to FY 2039-40; Greenfield and Brownfield), 3 (SGMZs on BHAVYA infrastructure) and 4 (hubs Meerut and Jalandhar) are correct - so only three.

s:
Consider the following statements about the RELIEF scheme for exporters:
1. RELIEF stands for Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation.
2. Its Component II was extended to 31 March 2027.
3. It is implemented by ECGC Ltd, set up in 1957 with headquarters in New Delhi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: ECGC Ltd (est. 1957) is headquartered in Mumbai. Statements 1 (full form) and 2 (Component II extended to 31 March 2027) are correct.

s:
With reference to the NITI Aayog-TEXMiN Statement of Intent (4 November 2026), consider the following statements:
1. TEXMiN is located at IIT (ISM) Dhanbad and is supported by the Department of Science and Technology.
2. The National Critical Mineral Mission has an expenditure of ₹18,000 crore.
3. NITI Aayog was established on 1 January 2015.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: NCMM's expenditure is ₹16,300 crore; ₹18,000 crore is the expected investment. Statements 1 (TEXMiN at IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, DST-supported) and 3 (NITI Aayog, 1 Jan 2015) are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 'Punah Bharan' groundwater-recharge app:
1. It was developed by BISAG-N, which works under the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
2. BISAG-N is headquartered at Gandhinagar.
3. Its partner, the National Water Mission, is one of the eight missions of the NAPCC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is wrong: BISAG-N works under MeitY (Ministry of Electronics and IT), not Jal Shakti. Statements 2 (HQ Gandhinagar) and 3 (National Water Mission, one of eight NAPCC missions) are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Vibrant Villages Programme (VVP):
1. It was launched in 2023 under the Ministry of Home Affairs, calling border villages the nation's "first villages".
2. VVP-II is a Central Sector scheme with 100% central funding.
3. VVP-I was launched at Nathanpur in Cachar district, Assam.
4. VVP-II leaves out whole States that were covered under VVP-I.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 3 and 4 are wrong: VVP-I was launched at Kibithoo, Anjaw (Arunachal Pradesh) - Nathanpur, Cachar (Assam) is where VVP-II was launched in 2026; and VVP-II leaves out only blocks already under VVP-I, not whole States. Statements 1 and 2 are correct.

s:
Match List I with List II (Vibrant Villages Programme):
List I
a. VVP-I outlay
b. VVP-II outlay
c. VVP-I villages
d. VVP-II villages
List II
i. 662
ii. ₹6,839 crore
iii. 1,954
iv. ₹4,800 crore
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: VVP-I: ₹4,800 crore for 662 villages (2022-23 to 2026-27); VVP-II: ₹6,839 crore for 1,954 villages (2024-25 to 2028-29). So a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. VVP-II covers 15 States and 2 UTs (Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh) on the other land borders.
2. MY Bharat volunteers living in border villages under the Viksit Vibrant Village Programme belong to the Ministry of Home Affairs.
3. The Border Area Development Programme began in 1986-87 on the eastern border.
4. India's longest land border is with Bangladesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 3 are wrong: MY Bharat is under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports; BADP began in 1986-87 on the western border. Statements 1 (15 States + 2 UTs) and 4 (Bangladesh) are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The People's Plan Campaign 2026-27 began on 2 October 2026 with the slogan "Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas".
2. Gram Panchayat Development Plans for FY 2027-28 are uploaded on eGramSwaraj.
3. PM Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana is a Central Sector Scheme of the Ministry of Rural Development.
4. PM Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana runs from 2026-27 to 2030-31, the 16th Finance Commission period.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: PM VGSY (₹7,395.55 crore, approved 29 Oct 2026) is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme and its nodal ministry is the Ministry of Panchayati Raj. Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct.

s:
Match List I with List II:
List I
a. 73rd Amendment came into force
b. Defines the Gram Sabha
c. Eleventh Schedule
d. Permissible works under the VB-G RAM G Act (Oct 2026)
List II
i. 375
ii. 29 subjects
iii. 24 April 1993
iv. Article 243(b)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: 73rd Amendment (1992) in force 24 April 1993; Article 243(b) defines the Gram Sabha; the 11th Schedule has 29 subjects; VB-G RAM G permissible rural works raised from 266 to 375. So a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.

s:
Assertion (A): Under the MoPR-CESL MoU (4 November 2026), EV charging and battery-swapping facilities will come up on Panchayat-owned land.
Reason (R): CESL is a wholly owned subsidiary of NTPC.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is true: the MoU is for EV charging and battery swapping on Panchayat-owned land. R is false: CESL is a wholly owned subsidiary of EESL, not NTPC.

s:
Under the Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana, match the old scheme (List I) with its new name (List II):
List I
a. IGNOAPS
b. IGNWPS
c. IGNDPS
d. NFBS
List II
i. PM Divyangjan Pension Yojana
ii. PM Parivar Labh Yojana
iii. PM Vriddhavastha Pension Yojana
iv. PM Vidhwa Pension Yojana
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: IGNOAPS - PM Vriddhavastha Pension Yojana; IGNWPS - PM Vidhwa Pension Yojana; IGNDPS - PM Divyangjan Pension Yojana; NFBS - PM Parivar Labh Yojana. So a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The National Social Assistance Programme, now renamed PMSSY, was launched on 15 August 1995 under the Ministry of Rural Development.
2. PMSSY has an outlay of ₹53,428 crore for 2026-27 to 2030-31.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: NSAP was launched on 15 August 1995 (Ministry of Rural Development) and was renamed PMSSY on 21 Oct 2026 with ₹53,428 crore for 2026-27 to 2030-31.

s:
Consider the following statements about Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY:
1. It was launched on 23 September 2018.
2. It gives a cover of ₹5 lakh per person per year.
3. Its beneficiaries are identified from the SECC.
4. 48.54 crore Ayushman Cards had been issued by 23 September 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: the ₹5 lakh cover is per family per year (family floater), not per person. Statements 1 (23 Sep 2018), 3 (SECC) and 4 (48.54 crore cards) are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements about the JOSH initiative under TB Mukt Bharat:
1. JOSH stands for Joint Squad for Health and was launched on 8 October 2026.
2. Its Phase 1 covers 55 districts in 15 States.
3. It uses the AI chatbot "Khushi Avatar".
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: Phase 1 covers 55 districts in 11 States. Statements 1 (Joint Squad for Health, 8 Oct 2026) and 3 (Khushi Avatar) are correct - so only two.

s:
Consider the following statements about TB elimination in India:
1. The PM TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan was launched on 9 September 2022.
2. The BPaLM regimen is used for drug-resistant TB.
3. The National TB Elimination Programme was earlier called RNTCP.
4. India's new TB case rate fell by 12% between 2015 and 2024.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statement 4 is wrong: India's new TB case rate fell by 21% between 2015 and 2024. Statements 1 (9 Sep 2022), 2 (BPaLM for drug-resistant TB) and 3 (NTEP was RNTCP) are correct.

s:
Assertion (A): India's target of eliminating Hepatitis B and C by 2030 is aligned with SDG 3.3.
Reason (R): The National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme was launched in 2018.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true (NVHCP, 2018, aims to eliminate Hepatitis B and C by 2030 under SDG 3.3), but the launch year of NVHCP does not explain why the target matches SDG 3.3 - so R is not the explanation of A.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The foundation stone of ICMR-CHAMP was laid on 12 October 2026 at Keylong, Lahaul and Spiti.
2. ICMR-CHAMP studies altitude illnesses such as AMS, HAPE and HACE.
3. ICMR, set up in 1911 as IRFA, works under the Department of Higher Education.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: ICMR (set up 1911 as IRFA, renamed 1949) is under the Department of Health Research. Statements 1 (Keylong, 12 Oct 2026) and 2 (AMS, HAPE, HACE) are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements about PM Vishwakarma:
1. It was launched on 17 September 2023 with the Ministry of MSME as nodal ministry.
2. Its outlay is ₹13,000 crore for 2023-24 to 2027-28.
3. It covers 21 traditional trades.
4. Its pillars are Samman, Samarthya and Samriddhi.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: PM Vishwakarma covers 18 traditional trades. Statements 1 (17 Sep 2023, Ministry of MSME), 2 (₹13,000 crore, 2023-24 to 2027-28) and 4 (Samman, Samarthya, Samriddhi) are correct - so only three.

s:
Match List I (PM Vishwakarma component) with List II (provision):
List I
a. Training stipend
b. Toolkit
c. Collateral-free loan
d. Interest on the loan
List II
i. Up to ₹3 lakh
ii. 5%
iii. ₹500 a day
iv. Up to ₹15,000
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Training stipend - ₹500 a day; toolkit - up to ₹15,000; collateral-free loan - up to ₹3 lakh; interest - 5%. So a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

s:
Consider the following statements about PM-SETU:
1. It is implemented by MSDE and was launched on 4 October 2025.
2. Its ₹60,000 crore outlay is made up of ₹30,000 crore from the Centre, ₹20,000 crore from States and ₹10,000 crore from industry.
3. The World Bank and ADB co-finance the entire central share.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: the World Bank and ADB co-finance 50% of the central share, not all of it. Statements 1 (MSDE, 4 Oct 2025) and 2 (₹30,000 + ₹20,000 + ₹10,000 crore = ₹60,000 crore) are correct.

2. The National Circular Bioenergy Scheme is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme of the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
3. The scheme has ₹23,731 crore for 2026-27 to 2035-36.
4. Its feedstock includes crop residue, cattle dung, press mud and mineral coal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 4 are wrong: the National Circular Bioenergy Scheme is a Central Sector Scheme of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, and its feedstock (crop residue, cattle dung, press mud, municipal organic waste) does not include mineral coal; it aims to raise CBG output about ten-fold. Statements 1 and 3 are correct.
